items.prompt:
Carrying capacity is the largest population an ecosystem can
A) support over time
B) destroy
C) ignore
D) create instantly

steps: Carrying capacity is the maximum supportable population.

items.prompt:
Which factor affects carrying capacity?
A) Amount of food
B) The color of the sky
C) The day of the week
D) The population's name

steps: Resources like food affect carrying capacity.

items.prompt:
On a population graph, the leveling-off value represents the
A) carrying capacity
B) starting population
C) number of species
D) temperature

steps: The flat level is the carrying capacity.

items.prompt:
Population growth slows near carrying capacity because
A) resources become limited
B) resources become unlimited
C) the species stops reproducing forever
D) the graph breaks

A drought that reduces water and plants will make the carrying capacity
A) increase
B) decrease
C) stay exactly the same
D) disappear

Which is a limiting factor?
A) Predators
B) Extra food
C) More space
D) More water

Why can a population not grow forever in an ecosystem?
A) A fixed resource supply feeds only a set number, the carrying capacity
B) Populations never grow
C) Resources are unlimited
D) There is no carrying capacity
items.answer: A) A fixed resource supply feeds only a set number, the carrying capacity

items.prompt:
If resources suddenly increase, a population's carrying capacity will
A) rise, allowing the population to grow larger
B) fall
C) vanish
D) stay the same no matter what
items.answer: A) rise, allowing the population to grow larger
